- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to underreact — increase forecast slightly to align with bullish momentum.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.25) in recent days, model often overcorrects downward — adjust forecast upward to avoid excessive bearish bias.  
- Model frequently underestimates late-period spikes (especially after 20–25 days) — apply a small upward bias to final 5–7 days of forecast.  
- Model shows persistent mean reversion bias — if price is trending sharply, forecast should not revert too quickly; allow 1–2 days of momentum before correction.  
- Overshoot after spikes (especially >70) is common — cap forecast at +5–10% above peak for next 3–5 days to avoid overcorrection.  
- If sentiment is flat (0.00) and price is trending, model often fails to capture momentum — add 0.5–1.0% lagged momentum adjustment to forecast.
